# Set44 independent reference and UI plan

Prepared November 17, 2026; planning only. D76/D77 have now been authorized: noon fixes roster membership, ownership/assignment, eligibility and current condition for that event, despite later edits/sale/retirement; required chain evidence is visibly awaited, never silently replaced or automatically cancelled; an event still unfinalized at the following Saturday lock enters the chain-incident path. Root is recording the exact decisions. This plan does not amend the frozen Set43 contract or generate any Set44 expected output.

Root's chosen foundation is **late authenticated per-participant capture**. Each original session may capture only its pinned gym; the bounded event remains incomplete until both fixed fixture participants have contributed. There is no fabricated session, unattended scheduler or claim that capture actually ran at noon. Chain anchoring/seed selection/finality are later dependencies, not features to invent in the reference or UI.

## Proposed finite corpus families

Exact DTO names, field order, domains, statuses, quotas and errors are **pending the reviewed contract**, not choices for the oracle. The following semantics can be planned independently now.

| Family | Required cases |
|---|---|
| Calendar | All 3,861 supported Saturday cutoffs; immediately before/equal/after cutoff and following-Saturday deadline; adjacent 167/168/169-hour spans, leap/year edges and unsupported dates. |
| Pins/IDs | Both existing fixture pins and their shared namespace; distinct per-gym contribution IDs; canonical ordering of declared participants; full source/store/calendar/rule/projector bindings. Cross-gym, cross-authority, wrong calendar/rule/descriptor substitutions refuse. |
| Historical roster | Empty initial state; complete sequential changes; no-op/abandoned/prepared rows; equal timestamps ordered by sequence; insert/remove/reinsert around cutoff; current roster different from the pre-cutoff roster. |
| Entry selection | Last committed saved entry strictly before cutoff, including withdrawal; prepared-only intent excluded; later observed closure does not become the cutoff. Source assignment must predate its historical roster insertion and selected cutoff. |
| Fence | Drain a pre-cutoff sampled write whose durable acknowledgement arrives later; durable highwater at least C; no C+1 requirement; equal-C roster changes excluded under proposed strict-prefix semantics; rollback refusal. |
| Stable historical prefix | Lawful post-C tail growth and post-C resolution of an old prepared intent do not invalidate sealed history. Changed/missing pre-C committed row, gap, duplicate sequence, impossible timestamp or selected receipt drift does. |
| Noon condition | Recompute from canonical original DNA and immutable birth at C with condition v1/XP0; distinguish save time, effective time C and actual capture/observation time T. Capture at C, C+1, hours/days later gives the same event condition. |
| Later changes | Post-C roster removal, current retirement and a synthetic future transfer leave frozen member/gym/condition bindings unchanged. No claim that Set44 implements a transfer service. |
| Contributions/event | First participant only remains incomplete; second completes the declared set; duplicate capture returns exact original bytes/digest; same identity with different payload refuses; participant order cannot change the canonical event root. Empty/withdrawn contribution is explicit, not a missing participant. |
| Crash/replay model | Prepared/fenced/captured/sealed boundaries as frozen by contract; uncertain pre/post-write outcomes and reopen lookup of exact identity; no auto-new contribution/root after lost ACK, no silent replacement of missing established state. |
| Incident timing | Authoritative observation at deadline−1, equality and +1; delayed/repeated observation, rollback/reopen; no automatic cancellation/reseed/new Saturday substitution. A calendar threshold is distinct from independently verified chain finality. |
| Protocol | Current complete view/store/event/participant/job binding, original capture author retained, ack/poll/cancel/unknown correlation, discovered job metadata, immutable terminal bytes, old-view/revoked responses and wrong participant rejected. |
| Bounds | Exact raw byte/depth/array/count limits; canonical scalar types and signed shoulder-jitter exception; capacity reserved for completion/reconciliation; cheap status paths perform no source hashing/rendering/simulation. |

For the last supported intake date, 2099-12-26, the following Saturday is in 2100. Recommend deriving that deadline from the same pinned calendar without admitting a new unsupported event date. Freeze this behavior explicitly; do not accidentally use EventForDate's old admitted-year rejection to erase D77's deadline.

Use `ZoneInfo.from_file` on the pinned bytes and separately cross-check integer Gregorian arithmetic plus the exact tail `PST8PDT,M3.2.0,M11.1.0`. The host zone database, browser clock and current civil-time law are not inputs. Keep timestamps as exact integers, and derive the following Saturday by local calendar date rather than adding 604,800,000 milliseconds across DST.

The canonical codec plan must rebuild **every** nested object in declared field order. For every accepted reordered/whitespace/escaped-key variant, compare its normalized expectation with an already independently constructed positive DTO, including nested job/view/fence/member objects. Include duplicate decoded keys, unknown/missing fields, integer spelling, malformed UTF-8/BOM, trailing values and maximum nested shapes. This directly addresses the two Set43 canonical-order defects without changing any old expectation.

## Source proof coverage and honest limits

The retained stable corpus has six genuine, independently proof-verified public-fixture receipts (three per gym), covering middle/light-heavy/heavy. Preserve all original birth/accepted facts and complete source-record digests. These give real source-backed selected-member input and both participant identities. Their proof verification happened in the prior oracle; simply reading them again is not a new Argon execution claim.

Five-class/max-cardinality examples and exact synthetic birth-at-retirement-boundary cases must remain labelled structural/state projections with assumed source facts, not admitted receipts. Actual Go integration must separately exercise concrete trusted-source verification. No fabricated source JSON, public receipt import, temporary date change or caller callback can grant assignment authority.

For real retained fighters, derive retirement comparisons at adjacent supported cutoffs using unchanged births. For exact C−1/C/C+1 career thresholds, use independently generated synthetic projection inputs explicitly separated from genuine receipts. Reuse the frozen integer/half-even condition oracle; no floating-point ratings, new condition version or fitted coefficients.

The state model can predict transcript/receipt facts and semantic write outcomes. It cannot prove LevelDB/fsync atomicity, process-kill recovery, source lifetime, actual account contention, pipe delivery or cleanup. Those need runtime tests with genuine lease gates, clocks and faults. Final packaged evidence must be independently rederived against its complete public inputs; development evidence remains distinct.

## UI integration proposal

Keep the same Saturday panel and existing entry history/draft. Add a visually separate event-snapshot/status area and bounded member details; do not change old closed Manifest/Stable/Entry frame shapes. Envelope proposes a separate closed Event protocol and job family on the shared one-active/one-queued lane. Final typed fields/states and the family's share of the existing aggregate 1MiB cache must be frozen before implementation.

| Situation | Proposed plain-language presentation and behavior |
|---|---|
| Before cutoff | Show the authority's Saturday/cutoff and current saved selection. Existing explicit Save/Replace/Withdraw continue. Snapshot says “Available after noon Pacific”; the browser cannot trigger closure by its own clock. |
| Cutoff passed; own capture absent | “Entries closed. Your noon snapshot is not recorded yet.” Offer the contract's authenticated capture action. It reads retained history, not the current draft; no automatic entry/mining or hidden other-account capture. |
| Capture queued/running | “Preparing your noon snapshot.” Cheap tracked-job polling; Stop/logout can invalidate and join work; no synchronous multi-proof stdin request blocking controls. |
| Own capture retained; other absent | “Your snapshot is saved. Waiting for the other fixture gym.” Show honest participant completion, not a complete league roster. Never fabricate the other session. |
| Event snapshot complete | Show “Candidate noon snapshot” with effective cutoff and actual capture times. Frozen eligibility/condition belong here; live fighter pages still show current roster/condition/retirement. |
| No chain adapter/evidence | “Snapshot saved. Chain anchoring and seed verification are not available in this candidate build.” No fake block/seed, progress percentage, fairness badge or finalized result. |
| Actual future adapter waiting/conflict | Use its authoritative typed state: “Waiting for the required chain evidence” / “Chain evidence conflicts; event is paused.” No reseed, automatic cancellation or silent replacement button. |
| Following-Saturday boundary | Show the contract's authority-observed candidate incident status with the no-seed/finality-authority limitation. Do not manufacture a verified public-chain incident from browser time or treat snapshot creation as event finality. |
| Unknown write | Retain event/contribution/operation identity; “Checking the recorded outcome.” Query first. No automatic new identity or changed payload. Cancelled display work does not claim a durable capture was undone. |
| Old route, stale view, unavailable | Keep the Saturday area explicitly unavailable; discard stale view data and pending automatic continuations. Do not silently migrate/adopt a missing journal or fall back to current roster as noon evidence. |

Historical receipt author/view remains inside an envelope bound to the current authorized view. Date changes, fixture switches, logout/reset, selection epoch changes and native modal pauses must prevent late results from replacing the visible event. An older event's recorded unknown outcome remains recoverable by exact identity, without executing its absent intent under new authorization.

DOM controls should cover both fixtures, held sessions, late capture after current retirement/roster edits, incomplete participant set, wrong-view terminal response, source/record drift, post-cutoff unknown ACK, immutable replay, following-Saturday DST boundaries, cache refusal and native-modal pause. Polling validates bounded metadata only: no proof, fight simulation, SVG regeneration or condition authority from JavaScript. Keep fixed inventory pages/Follow Recent and preview caches working under reciprocal capacity checks. No visual/native chooser/screen-reader or D74 completion claim follows from DOM tests.

## Freeze prerequisites and next steps

Before generation, the core contract must fix historical prefix/fence evidence, exact same-ms boundary, event/participant identities, current-versus-original author rules, trusted ownership/assignment projection and the meaning/source of `unfinalized`. The helper contract must fix capture activation, current-view wrappers, deadline/incident status without a chain adapter, async cancellation and cache/transport bounds. These are concrete engineering choices, not reasons for another player questionnaire.

Then copy/pin approved inputs, author only the independent reference, create a finite corpus with explicit real/synthetic provenance, and run deterministic byte checks under two absolute Python interpreters and distinct host TZ settings. Preserve inputs/source/output hashes and separate independent review; only after freeze compare runtime. No new reference execution, new Go reads or implementation work has been performed for this plan.
